title: Direct view of exciton and carrier dynamics in twisted bilayer graphene
authors: Gianmarco Gatti, Anders S. Mortensen, Zhihao Jiang, Alfred J. H. Jones, Gesa-R. Siemann, Thomas S. Nielsen, Søren Ulstrup, Naina Kushwaha, Bruce Weaver, Yu Zhang, Emma Springate, Charlotte E. Sanders, Vibha Reddy, Ulrich Starke, Philip Hofmann
abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) on H-intercalated SiC (twist angle of $9 \pm 1^{\circ}$) is studied by position\mbox{-}, time\mbox{-}, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). Both graphene layers are hole doped, with a Dirac-point offset of 30~meV. Time-resolved ARPES near the van Hove singularity reveals a spectral feature within the hybridization-induced band gap, together with excited electrons in the conduction band. The in-gap feature exhibits distinct dynamics, and its binding energy and $k$-space location are consistent with the proposed non-hydrogenic ``ghost-Fano'' exciton arising from destructive interference between two nearly degenerate excitonic channels. Near the Dirac points, the twist separates the largely layer-polarized Dirac cones in momentum space, providing direct layer selectivity. We find markedly different peak electronic temperatures in the two graphene layers, even though their subsequent cooling dynamics are very similar. We attribute this to an ultrafast interlayer redistribution of electronic energy, driven by an interlayer electric field that arises from the different doping in the layers.
summary: This work uses time-resolved ARPES to probe exciton and carrier dynamics in twisted bilayer graphene. Key findings include the direct observation of a 'ghost-Fano' exciton and the demonstration that doping differences induce an ultrafast, field-driven energy transfer between the two graphene layers, leading to distinct electronic temperature profiles.
main_problem: The study investigates the ultrafast dynamics of excitons and charge carriers in twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) to understand energy relaxation mechanisms.
main_result: The research identified a 'ghost-Fano' exciton signature and revealed an ultrafast, field-driven energy redistribution, causing the two graphene layers to reach significantly different peak electronic temperatures.
method: Time-resolved angle- and position-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used, coupled with fitting models like the three-temperature model.
model_or_system: The system is twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) on SiC at a specific twist angle. The analysis models carrier and energy relaxation using a three-temperature framework ($T_e, T_p, T_l$) and incorporates concepts like interlayer electric fields and excitonic resonances.
key_observables: Exciton binding energy, exciton lifetime ($	au_X$), peak electronic temperatures ($T_e$), and the time evolution of these temperatures.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($9 \pm 1^\circ$), doping offsets (e.g., 30 meV), and the interlayer electric field strength ($\approx 0.1 	ext{ V/nm}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting experimental spectra using the finite-slit Fermi-edge model and the three-temperature model, assuming the energy transfer is field-biased and ultrafast.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate sample characterization, exciton/carrier dynamics at the van Hove singularity, and time-dependent electronic temperature evolution for the top and bottom layers, fitted to a three-temperature model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from characterizing the system and observing the exciton signature (ghost-Fano exciton) to analyzing the layer-dependent electronic temperature dynamics, culminating in the attribution of temperature asymmetry to interlayer energy transfer driven by doping differences.
why_interesting: The study provides experimental evidence of non-equilibrium energy transfer and correlation effects (excitons) in a tunable 2D material system, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated electronic states in novel quantum materials.
